page.title: GitHub · Change is constant. GitHub keeps you ahead. · GitHub · GitHub

findings.title: One h2 is a different size from the other 9
findings.evidence: “COMPANIES USING GITHUB” is 14px; the other h2s are 24/34/40px (14px ×1, 24px ×5, 34px ×2, 40px ×2). Same semantic level should get the same treatment.
findings.fix: Pick one size for h2 and set it once in CSS. If one of these is really a sub-heading, change its tag instead of its size.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: Card is far taller than its content
findings.evidence: div.Testimonials__stat__Mnxlqt is 455×330px but its content occupies 13% of that; 81px of empty space sits under the last line. Nothing inside it needs the height, so a fixed height or min-height is probably set.
findings.fix: Remove the fixed height / min-height and let the card size to its content, or fill the space with something that earns it.
findings.citation: Lin 2004: whitespace helps comprehension when it frames content; dead space inside a container just reads as unfinished

findings.title: 4 cards in a row stretched to the tallest one
findings.evidence: All 4 are 579px tall, but content ends at 571, 411, 331, 451px from the top. Empty space below content: 8, 168, 249, 128px. One card's wrapped text is dictating the height of its siblings.
findings.fix: Either shorten the long one so they match naturally, align content to the top and accept a little empty space, or use align-items: start so cards hug their content. Avoid a row where two tiles are 60% air.
findings.citation: Gestalt: items given equal size are read as equal weight — empty tiles read as padding

findings.title: AI purple accent
findings.evidence: 5 elements use a violet/indigo accent (hue 260–310°), e.g. a.RepositoryPanel__9cDraF. This is the single most-cited vibe-coded tell in the Reddit corpus (#2 overall).
findings.fix: Pick one base hue that means something for this product and derive the palette from it. If you keep purple, make it a decision: one accent, solid, used sparingly.

findings.title: Head is missing: title is 70 chars (cuts off ~60)
findings.evidence: No JSON-LD structured data either, so AI search engines have nothing to cite. One h1, good.
findings.fix: Ten minutes of <head> work: title under 60 chars, canonical URL, lang attribute, favicon, and an Organization or WebSite JSON-LD block.

findings.title: 149 words under 12px on a phone
findings.evidence: 16 text blocks render below 12px at 390px, e.g. p.RepositoryDescription__JVXrci “Hyprland is an independent, highly custo…” at 11px.
findings.fix: Body text 16px on mobile; nothing readable under 12px. If the desktop size is in px, use clamp() or a mobile breakpoint.

findings.title: Marketing buzzword
findings.evidence: “3 buzzword phrases: "ed Security Enterprise-grade code securi"”
findings.fix: Generic SaaS phrases (streamline / empower / supercharge / world-class / enterprise-grade / next-generation / cutting-edge / etc) are instant AI tells. Pick a specific verb and noun that says what the product literally does.

findings.title: Frosted-glass panels (2)
findings.evidence: 2 elements combine backdrop-filter blur with a translucent background, e.g. a.Primer_Brand__Button-module__Button___scH9Z.Primer_Brand__Button-module__Button--secondary___gHnw_. On 17% of Show HN launches.
findings.fix: Use a solid surface. Translucency only earns its place when something meaningful is behind it.

findings.title: Centered hero: big headline, centered sub, centered buttons
findings.evidence: h1 at 56px, centered, with 2 centered blocks under it. On 23.5% of Show HN launches. It's the layout every builder emits when nobody chooses one.
findings.fix: Not a problem on its own, but combined with other tells it's the skeleton. Left-align and put the product next to the headline, or lead with the product itself.

findings.title: h3 is used at 3 sizes, consistently
findings.evidence: Sizes: 20px ×5, 22px ×3, 28px ×2. “GitHub” is 28px, “Actions” is 20px. Each size is used more than once, so this is a system rather than drift; but it means the same tag is doing two jobs.
findings.fix: If the 20px ones are sub-sections, make them h4. Screen readers and search engines only see the tag.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: 4 status dots on the page
findings.evidence: Coloured dots attached to labels where a word would say more.
